source_refs.note: Chapter 5 exercise as printed (PDF 150-152, printed 147-149); MCQs, short and long questions as printed; answers only in the Roman Urdu lesson.

blocks.text: 1. Which of the following is an example of a basic statistical model?

items: a) Linear Regression
b) Neural Networks
c) Decision Trees
d) Support Vector Machines

blocks.text: 2. What does experimental design in data science involve?

items: a) Creating visualizations
b) Collecting and analyzing data systematically
c) Writing code for machine learning
d) Building databases

blocks.text: 3. Which of the following is NOT a type of data visualization?

items: a) Bar Chart
b) Scatter Plot
c) Hypothesis Test
d) Heatmap

blocks.text: 4. Which tool is commonly used for creating data visualizations?

items: a) MS Excel
b) Python (Matplotlib)
c) Tableau
d) All of the above

blocks.text: 5. What does the slope in a linear regression model represent?

items: a) The intercept of the model
b) The change in the dependent variable for a unit change in the independent variable
c) The error term
d) The mean of the data

blocks.text: 6. Which of the following is an example of a real-world application of statistical models?

items: a) Predicting house prices
b) Creating social media posts
c) Designing websites
d) Writing essays

blocks.text: 7. Which of the following is NOT a benefit of data visualization?

items: a) Identifying trends and patterns
b) Communicating insights effectively
c) Making data more complex
d) Summarizing large datasets

blocks.text: 8. What is the primary goal of K-Means Clustering?

items: a) To classify data into predefined categories
b) To group data into clusters based on similarity
c) To predict continuous outcomes
d) To reduce the dimensionality of data

blocks.text: 9. In K-Means Clustering, what does the "K" represent?

items: a) The number of features in the dataset
b) The number of clusters to be formed
c) The number of iterations required for convergence
d) The number of data points in the dataset
